evidence: Closed in 7f7817f990. Added a signature-compatible behavioural red test that drives the production default derivation path (no system_presence kwarg, no _bank_system_presence reference), so it is callable against the pre-fix signature and fails there for a BEHAVIOURAL reason: AssertionError, assert 24 == 0 on the no_prefix_mismatch list (the exact rc=23 halt content), not a missing-symbol death. It asserts on report CONTENT (n_violations == 0, n_no_prefix_asymmetry_expected == 24, 12 rows per direction, per-row no_prefix_side == system_absent_side, n_pairs_checked == 36) rather than on passed alone, closing the trap that a passed-only assert cannot distinguish a SKIPPED pe-check from one that ran. Reverse A-bare coverage added in both the excused and the still-HALTing form; the frozen bank also realizes the A-bare direction natively (v2 is side A in all 12 v2-v3 pairs), so both directions are exercised on the production path. Both reviewers independently reproduced the behavioural red; Claude additionally simulated a signature-PRESERVING revert (excuse neutered to if False, kwarg and report keys retained) and confirmed the new test catches it, which was the precise gap this finding named. Disclosed and accepted: the 7 original round-4 pins remain signature-artifact-only as written; the finding closes via the ADDED behavioural coverage, not by rewriting them.

evidence: Closed in 0e870ae0cf. The temp unlink inside the except BaseException handler is now best-effort: an inner except OSError logs a warning and the bare raise then proceeds, so the ORIGINAL write/replace exception propagates unchanged. Verified across every failure combination: write-fail, replace-fail, unlink-fail, and write-and-unlink both failing. The reviewer confirmed the IDENTICAL exception object escapes (e is orig is True) with __context__ and __cause__ undisturbed and the original raise site still on the traceback, that a non-OSError cleanup failure (KeyboardInterrupt) still escapes rather than being suppressed, and that the happy path performs exactly one os.replace with zero residue. The except OSError cleanup scope was judged correct rather than widened: Path.unlink's realistic surface is all OSError, and KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit / MemoryError should escape cleanup. Pre-change red was BEHAVIOURAL, verbatim: Expected regex 'simulated replace failure' / Actual message 'simulated unlink failure'. A follow-on fold (ece87f8704) binds the cleanup exception into the warning so a production firing can distinguish EACCES / EROFS / EIO, which the path-only message could not.

summary: Closed in 0e870ae0cf. The pin now writes the SAME destination twice within one process and asserts the two captured temp names differ. Because basename and pid are then shared, only a genuinely...
evidence: Closed in 0e870ae0cf. The pin now writes the SAME destination twice within one process and asserts the two captured temp names differ. Because basename and pid are then shared, only a genuinely per-call uuid draw can satisfy it. Verified to BITE rather than merely to pass: against a scratch variant with uuid4().hex[:8] replaced by a constant, the assertion fails with two identical names (a.json.<pid>.deadbeef.tmp twice), so a uuid hoisted to module scope or otherwise made constant can no longer pass. The original vacuous comparison, which compared three paths whose destination basenames already differed (a.json, b.jsonl, c.pt) and would therefore have passed with a constant uuid, was removed. The pid-bearing shape pin for all three writers was retained.

summary: Post-regen emit_cap_hit_report(cfg, scope) (issue2329_run.py:3703/:3964) overwrites the canonical driving report at the RAISED cap: legacy rows lacking per-row max_new_tokens are misattributed via...
evidence: Post-regen emit_cap_hit_report(cfg, scope) (issue2329_run.py:3703/:3964) overwrites the canonical driving report at the RAISED cap: legacy rows lacking per-row max_new_tokens are misattributed via the :3276 fallback and the report-level cap becomes 4096 (:3368). Consequences: (1) Phase B (rest) capregen and any crashed-worker re-invocation are refused by _load_breach_report (:3535-3541), and the refusal's suggested 8192 escalation then dies at the cross-regime refusal (base_fp computed at 4096 vs 2048 done records) — the designed Phase A->Phase B flow cannot execute; (2) the natural recovery (re-run --phase cap_report at default cap) recomputes breaching_cells over the mixed pooled store (cell_counts keys on cell only, :3283) and can silently drop cells whose remaining rows are still truncated — #779-class under-regeneration of the primary F_beh inputs, deviating from the registered per-cell remedy; (3) realized_caps_by_batch/realized_row_caps are corrupted in every post-regen report (a half-done Phase A reads gate:[4096], indistinguishable from complete); (4) a completed grid capregen's idempotent re-entry raises instead of skipping. Evidence: worktree issue-2329, commits 22d70f009c+f0255552a7; pre-diff code writes no per-row max_new_tokens (git show a79bb354b7). Fix: emit post-regen reports at the BASE cap (replace(cfg, max_new_tokens=base_cap)) AND write them to a non-canonical sibling path (cap_hit_report_<scope>_postregen.json) so the driving report is never clobbered; add a Phase A->Phase B sequence test.
